profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a global bank's Strategy and Regulatory Office to align the Regulatory Analytics and Legal Entity Data Governance workstreams on a board pre-read about using the firm's legal-entity control hierarchy as a proxy for organizational complexity relative to peer SIFIs. The Chief Risk Officer wants a concise update before the quarterly Legal Entity Simplification Committee, and the two teams need to coordinate the hierarchy snapshot, the complexity score materials, the appendix on year-over-year changes, and the shared folder posting. The agenda is to confirm which hierarchy baseline will feed the analysis, what is included in the 'complexity pack,' how this quarter's simplification actions will be represented, and what will be posted to the shared committee folder by Friday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs: Data Governance will provide the hierarchy-related materials, Regulatory Analytics will prepare the committee-facing analysis, and both will believe they have aligned on the package to be finalized for the committee.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: prudential regulation, bank structural metrics, board reporting
members.background: Elena has spent nine years in bank risk strategy, first in stress testing and later in resolution-planning analytics, and now leads the team that converts legal-entity data into senior-management and regulator-facing complexity metrics.
members.private_state: She needs a clean, defensible narrative showing that the firm's structural complexity has continued to trend down, while avoiding any last-minute disputes over methodology or source timing that could delay the board pre-read.
hidden_assumptions: When senior management asks for the 'current hierarchy,' they mean the latest quarter-end certified hierarchy because committee and regulatory materials must tie to an auditable reporting point.
When people say the 'complexity pack,' they naturally mean the committee-facing set of materials built around the metrics output: slides, score tables, and a short appendix in the usual format.

This quarter's 'changes' should only include legal-entity actions that were fully effective in the certified ledger by quarter end, because only those count as realized complexity reduction for committee reporting.
Posting the 'final package' to the shared folder means uploading the committee-ready deck and appendix after the underlying hierarchy file has been incorporated and lightly formatted.
If Data Governance says a file is ready, any remaining differences are likely metadata or administrative refreshes rather than changes that would alter the board narrative.

members.name: Marcus Vale
members.role: Head of Legal Entity Data Governance
members.expertise: entity master data, corporate structure records, governance controls
members.background: Marcus came from corporate secretary operations and now runs the team responsible for the bank's legal-entity master, subsidiary relationship records, controlled hierarchy snapshots, and governed distribution to downstream users.
members.private_state: He wants to reinforce that his team is the authoritative source for structural data, ensure downstream consumers use the freshest governed extract available, and avoid being blamed if reporting teams build committee materials off an older snapshot.
hidden_assumptions: The 'current hierarchy' obviously means the latest monthly operational extract from the entity master, because that is the most up-to-date representation of the group's structure.
The 'complexity pack' is the governed hierarchy bundle that supports any analysis: the hierarchy extract, entity-type mapping, exclusions note, and change log.

This quarter's 'changes' should include approved and operationally loaded simplification actions even if some final legal clean-up or certification steps are still pending, because the managed structure has already moved.
Posting the 'final package' means publishing the governed hierarchy bundle to the shared folder so every downstream team works from the same official source package.
If the committee materials are based on the official hierarchy bundle in the folder, then any presentation-layer versioning is secondary and does not redefine what the final package is.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to use the 'current hierarchy' for the board pre-read.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the quarter-end certified hierarchy snapshot dated March 31, because that matches prior committee materials and is auditable for regulatory purposes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the latest monthly operational hierarchy snapshot dated April 30, because that is the freshest governed view and already includes recently loaded entity changes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this bank, both snapshots come from the same legal-entity source team and are routinely described as the hierarchy, so the adjective 'current' feels like harmless shorthand rather than a meaningful choice of reporting basis.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to finalize the 'complexity pack' by Thursday so Friday is just for circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the 'complexity pack' is the committee-facing materials: the slide deck, complexity score tables, and appendix in the standard committee format, with the hierarchy extract as an input rather than part of the pack itself.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the 'complexity pack' is the governed support bundle: hierarchy extract, mapping tabs, exclusions note, and change log, which together constitute the package that should be finalized before anyone circulates outputs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like an established shared artifact and both teams have used it informally in previous cycles, but each side anchors the package around its own work product layer, so the shared label creates false consensus without triggering clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss showing 'this quarter's simplification changes' in the appendix.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 will count only entities fully dissolved, merged, or re-parented in the certified ledger by quarter end, because that is what counts as completed simplification in committee reporting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 will count approved and operationally loaded dissolutions, re-parentings, and booked clean-up actions during the quarter, even if some legal or certification steps complete afterward.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are aligned on the general goal of demonstrating simplification progress, and 'this quarter's changes' sounds like a routine status phrase; the disagreement is buried in the threshold for when a change is considered real enough to count.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'final package' posted Friday refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to post the 'final package' to the shared folder by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means Regulatory Analytics will upload the committee-ready PDF deck and appendix workbook after incorporating Marcus's hierarchy file into the analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means Data Governance will upload the governed hierarchy bundle, and the committee materials will be downstream outputs that simply reference that official folder content.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both strongly endorse a single source of truth and a clean Friday handoff, so agreeing on a 'final package' feels like operational alignment; the ambiguity survives because one is thinking about the final committee-consumption artifact while the other is thinking about the final governed input bundle.
